latest_nl_proof:
We prove a stronger statement by induction on r. For each positive integer r, let P(r) be: for every positive integer n there exists a vector w_{n,r}=(w_1,...,w_n) of positive integers with w_1>w_2>...>w_n such that for every real vector x=(x_1,...,x_n), Total(T_{Alt_r^+}(x)) = sum_{i=1}^n w_i x_i and Total(T_{Alt_r^-}(x)) = sum_{i=1}^n w_{n+1-i} x_i. The lemma is exactly P(r) with n=m.

Base case r=1. Here Alt_1^+=(+1) and Alt_1^-=(-1), so T_{Alt_1^+}(x)=U(x) and T_{Alt_1^-}(x)=D(x). If x has length n, then by the definitions of U and D, Total(U(x)) = sum_{j=1}^{n+1} sum_{i=1}^{j-1} x_i = sum_{i=1}^n (n+1-i)x_i, because x_i appears in U(x)_j exactly when j>i, namely for n+1-i values of j. Likewise, Total(D(x)) = sum_{j=1}^{n+1} sum_{i=j}^{n} x_i = sum_{i=1}^n i x_i, because x_i appears in D(x)_j exactly when j<=i, namely for i values of j. Therefore P(1) holds with w_{n,1}=(n,n-1,...,1), which is a strictly decreasing vector of positive integers.

Inductive step. Assume P(r) holds for some r>=1. Fix a positive integer n. Apply P(r) with length n+1, and denote the resulting vector by v=(v_1,...,v_{n+1})=w_{n+1,r}. Then v_1>v_2>...>v_{n+1}>0, and for every real vector z of length n+1, Total(T_{Alt_r^+}(z)) = sum_{j=1}^{n+1} v_j z_j and Total(T_{Alt_r^-}(z)) = sum_{j=1}^{n+1} v_{n+2-j} z_j.

Define a length n vector w=(w_1,...,w_n) by w_i = sum_{k=1}^{n+1-i} v_k for 1<=i<=n. Since each v_k is a positive integer, each w_i is a positive integer. Also, for 1<=i<n, w_i-w_{i+1} = v_{n+1-i}>0, so w_1>w_2>...>w_n.

Now let x be any real vector of length n. Deleting the first sign from Alt_{r+1}^+ leaves Alt_r^-, so by the recursive definition of T_t, T_{Alt_{r+1}^+}(x)=T_{Alt_r^-}(U(x)). Hence Total(T_{Alt_{r+1}^+}(x)) = sum_{j=1}^{n+1} v_{n+2-j} U(x)_j = sum_{j=1}^{n+1} v_{n+2-j} sum_{i=1}^{j-1} x_i = sum_{i=1}^n (sum_{j=i+1}^{n+1} v_{n+2-j}) x_i = sum_{i=1}^n w_i x_i, because sum_{j=i+1}^{n+1} v_{n+2-j} = sum_{k=1}^{n+1-i} v_k = w_i.

Similarly, deleting the first sign from Alt_{r+1}^- leaves Alt_r^+, so T_{Alt_{r+1}^-}(x)=T_{Alt_r^+}(D(x)). Therefore Total(T_{Alt_{r+1}^-}(x)) = sum_{j=1}^{n+1} v_j D(x)_j = sum_{j=1}^{n+1} v_j sum_{i=j}^{n} x_i = sum_{i=1}^{n} (sum_{j=1}^{i} v_j) x_i. But by the definition of w, w_{n+1-i} = sum_{k=1}^{i} v_k. Thus Total(T_{Alt_{r+1}^-}(x)) = sum_{i=1}^{n} w_{n+1-i} x_i.

So P(r+1) holds. By induction, P(r) is true for every positive integer r. Taking n=m gives the required vector w_{m,r}, and the lemma follows.
role_in_parent: This is a support lemma for L5; it converts alternating continuations into explicit dot products so that rearrangement can be applied.
statement_nl: Fix positive integers m and r. For a vector x of length m and a sign string t=(t_1,...,t_r) with each t_q in {+1,-1}, define x^(0)=x and for q=1,...,r define x^(q) by x^(q)=U(x^(q-1)) when t_q=+1 and x^(q)=D(x^(q-1)) when t_q=-1, where for any vector y=(y_1,...,y_ell), the vectors U(y) and D(y) of length ell+1 are given by U(y)_j = sum_{i=1}^{j-1} y_i and D(y)_j = sum_{i=j}^{ell} y_i for 1 <= j <= ell+1, with empty sums equal to 0. Write T_t(x)=x^(r). Let Alt_r^+=(+1,-1,+1,-1,...) and Alt_r^-=(-1,+1,-1,+1,...) be the two alternating sign strings of length r. Then there exists a vector w_{m,r}=(w_1,...,w_m) of positive integers with w_1 > w_2 > ... > w_m such that for every real vector x=(x_1,...,x_m), Total(T_{Alt_r^+}(x)) = sum_{i=1}^m w_i x_i and Total(T_{Alt_r^-}(x)) = sum_{i=1}^m w_{m+1-i} x_i, where Total(y) denotes the sum of the entries of y.

domain_restrictions: m and r are positive integers.
The input vector x has exactly m entries.
Each sign t_q is either plus one or minus one.
For a generic vector y of length ell, U(y) and D(y) have length ell plus 1.
The coefficients w_1 through w_m are positive integers.
The coefficients satisfy strict decrease: w_1 greater than w_2 greater than ... greater than w_m.
The final identities are required for every real vector x of length m.
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For each positive integers m and r, there exists a strictly decreasing sequence of positive integers w_1 through w_m, depending only on m and r, such that for every real vector x of length m, the total sum of the entries after applying the alternating plus-first sign pattern r times equals the linear form with coefficients w_1 through w_m, and the total sum after applying the alternating minus-first sign pattern r times equals the linear form with the same coefficients in reversed order.
quantifier_order: Fix positive integers m and r.
For every sign string t of length r with entries plus one or minus one, the recursive map T_t is defined on vectors of length m.
There exists a vector w_{m,r} of length m with positive integer entries such that w_1 is greater than w_2 and so on down to w_m.
For every real vector x of length m, the two stated identities hold for the alternating sign strings of length r.

variables.name: r
variables.role: fixed parameter controlling the number of sign steps

variables.name: x
variables.role: input vector for the transformation and the linear identities

variables.domain: strings of length r with entries plus one or minus one
variables.name: t
variables.role: controls whether each step applies U or D

variables.name: q
variables.role: step index in the recursive definition

variables.name: y
variables.role: generic input to U and D

variables.name: ell
variables.role: length of the generic vector y

variables.name: i
variables.role: summation index in the formulas for U, D, and the final linear forms

variables.name: j
variables.role: coordinate index in U(y) and D(y)

variables.name: w
variables.role: coefficient vector whose existence is asserted

witness_dependencies: The witness vector w_{m,r} may depend on m and r.
The witness does not depend on the particular choice of x.
The same witness vector must work simultaneously for both alternating sign strings Alt_r^+ and Alt_r^-.
